# Additions to Esther Chapter 3 (Addition C) — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther C | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_003_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition C: The prayers of Mordecai and Esther. This is the theological heart of Greek Esther — God is finally, explicitly named. Mordecai explains why he would not bow to Haman. Esther's prayer is raw, bodily, intimate: she hates the royal crown, hates sharing a bed with an uncircumcised man, weeps before God stripped of every royal pretension.]*

**1** Then Mordecai prayed to the Lord. He called to mind everything the Lord had done, and he said:

**2** "O Lord, Lord, you are the almighty King. Everything exists within your power. There is no one who can stand against you when you decide to save Israel.

**3** You made heaven and earth and every wonder that lies beneath the sky.

**4** You are Lord over everything. No one can withstand you, Lord — no one.

**5** You know everything. And Lord, you know this: what I did — refusing to bow to that arrogant Haman — I did not do it out of pride or arrogance, or to make myself look important.

**6** I would have been perfectly willing to kiss the soles of his feet if it meant saving Israel.

**7** But I would not set a human being's honor above the honor of God. I will bow to no one but you — you who are my God and my Lord. I will not do this out of pride.

**8** So now, O Lord, God and King, God of Abraham — have mercy on your people. Eyes are fixed on us with intent to destroy us; they want to wipe out the inheritance that has been yours since the very beginning.

**9** Do not abandon the portion that you redeemed for yourself out of Egypt.

**10** Hear my prayer. Show mercy to your inheritance. Turn our mourning into celebration, so that we may live and praise your name. Lord — do not close the mouths of those who praise you."

**11** And all Israel cried out with all their strength, because death stared them in the face.

**12** Queen Esther was seized with terror. She fled to the Lord.

**13** She stripped off her magnificent robes and put on clothes of grief and mourning. Instead of costly perfumes she put ashes and dung on her head. She humbled her body completely. Every part of her that she had adorned for joyful occasions she now covered with the wild tangle of her unbound hair.

**14** And she prayed to the Lord God of Israel. She said:

**15** "My Lord — you alone are our King. Help me. I am alone. There is no one else to help me but you.

**16** My danger is here, right now, in my own hands.

**17** From the time I was a child, I heard it in my family's tribe: you, Lord, chose Israel out of all the peoples of the earth, and you chose our ancestors out of all their forebears, as an inheritance that would last forever. And you kept every single promise you made to them.

**18** But we sinned against you. And you handed us over to our enemies,

**19** because we gave glory to their gods. And you were right to do it, Lord. You were completely right.

**20** But they are still not satisfied with the bitterness of our slavery. Now they have joined forces with their idols

**21** to erase the decree that came from your mouth — to destroy your inheritance, to silence the mouths that praise you, to put out the glory of your house and your altar,

**22** and to open the mouths of the nations to praise their empty idols, and to magnify a mortal king forever.

**23** Do not hand over your scepter, Lord, to things that have no existence. Do not let them mock us in our destruction. Turn their own schemes back on their heads. Make an example of the one who started all of this.

**24** Remember us, Lord. Show yourself in the time of our suffering. Give me courage — you, the King of all gods, the Master of every realm.

**25** Put the right words in my mouth when I stand before the lion. Turn his heart so that he hates the one who is fighting us, so that he and all those who agree with him come to their end.

**26** Rescue us by your own hand. Help me — I am alone, I have no one but you, Lord.

**27** You know everything. And you know this: I hate the glory of the lawless. I abhor the bed of the uncircumcised — of any foreigner.

**28** You know what I am constrained to do. I hate that sign of arrogance they make me wear on my head on the days when I have to appear in public. I hate it the way you hate a cloth of menstruation. I do not wear it on my days of quiet and rest.

**29** And I have not eaten at Haman's table. I have not honored the king's feasts. I have not drunk the wine of their libations.

**30** From the day I was placed here until this moment, your servant has known no joy — only in you, Lord God of Abraham.

**31** O God, who are more powerful than all, hear the voice of those who have lost all hope. Save us from the hand of evil people. And deliver me from my fear."
